narration.text: Why Earth couldn't hold a volcano 2.5 times Everest.
Mars's Olympus Mons stands about 21 kilometres high.
It's about 600 kilometres wide, the size of Italy in area.
So standing on it, you'd barely notice you're on a mountain.
On Earth, crust this tall would sink and crumble under its weight.
Mars' weaker gravity and still crust let it grow.
So the Solar System's giant volcano needed a smaller planet.
